regions.name: Dustbowl Flats
regions.description: Sun-baked farmland and roadside ruins around the homestead.

enemies.name: glare-rat
encounter: A glare-rat is staring at me. It glows faintly. So, now, do I, probably.
Spotted a glare-rat. Big as a cat. Brave as a much bigger cat.
win: Chased off a glare-rat. It squeaked something unkind about my mother.
Beat a glare-rat with a little help from my boot.
retreat: The glare-rat bit my ankle and I left the area at speed.
Lost a fight to a rat. Moving on. Nobody needs to know.

enemies.name: cloud of dust gnats
encounter: A cloud of dust gnats found me. Or I found them. Either way, nobody's happy.
Walked into a swarm of dust gnats. They're in my ears. They're in my everything.
win: Outlasted the dust gnats. I think they got bored of me.
Swatted my way out of a gnat cloud. Victory tastes like gnats.
retreat: Fled the gnats. They followed me for a mile, humming judgementally.
The gnats won. I ran. I'm still itching in places I can't reach.

enemies.name: scrap hound
encounter: A scrap hound is trotting towards me. Its collar says 'Buddy'. Buddy is not a buddy anymore.
Spotted a scrap hound nosing through junk. It smelled me first, and I smell strongly.
win: Sent the scrap hound packing. Good boy. Bad boy. Gone boy.
The scrap hound lost interest after I hit it with a hubcap.
retreat: The scrap hound chewed on me for a while. I climbed a car and waited it out.
Man's best friend just ruined my trousers. Retreating.

enemies.name: lone Skitter
encounter: A Skitter clicked at me from under a porch.
One Skitter. Where there's one Skitter there are forty. Staying alert.
win: Stomped a Skitter. It made a noise like a dropped bag of crisps.
Dealt with a Skitter. Legs everywhere. None of them mine.
retreat: The Skitter ran up my leg and I ran everywhere else.
Lost to a bug. A big bug. But still, technically, a bug.

enemies.name: tin-can crab
encounter: Something is living in a paint can and it has claws. A tin-can crab.
A tin-can crab is waving its pincers at me in what I assume is not a greeting.
win: Evicted the tin-can crab. Kept the can.
Cracked the tin-can crab's shell. Smells like low tide and motor oil.
retreat: The tin-can crab pinched me somewhere I will not be writing down. Leaving.
The crab won. The crab lives in a soup can. I lost to soup.

enemies.name: Burrower pup
encounter: A Burrower pup popped out of the ground. Cute, if you like teeth.
The ground is wriggling. It's a Burrower pup. Its mother is hopefully elsewhere.
win: Shooed the Burrower pup back into its hole. It sulked.
The Burrower pup gave up and dug away. Mother not sighted. Grateful.
retreat: The Burrower pup took a chunk out of me. Retreating before it fetches the family.
Lost to a baby. A baby with a jaw like a bear trap, but still.

enemies.name: Rustman scout
encounter: A Rustman scout is watching me through a spyglass made from two bottle necks.
Spotted a Rustman scout. He spotted me too. Awkward for everyone.
win: The Rustman scout ran off to tell his friends. His friends will be disappointed.
Beat a Rustman scout. He had a list of 'targets'. I was on it. I crossed myself off.
retreat: The Rustman scout shot at me with something rusty. I left before the tetanus set in.
Retreated from a Rustman scout. He yelled 'And stay out!' This is not his property.

enemies.name: Hollowed wanderer
encounter: A Hollowed is wandering the road, humming a jingle from before the Glare.
Saw a Hollowed standing at a bus stop, patiently waiting for a bus that isn't coming.
win: Put the Hollowed to rest. I finished humming its jingle for it.
The Hollowed went down. I hope it caught its bus.
retreat: The Hollowed grabbed me with a very cold hand. I ran. I'm still cold.
Couldn't handle the Hollowed. It's still humming. I can hear it from here.

enemies.name: carrion kite
encounter: A carrion kite is circling overhead. I'm trying to look extremely alive.
Big bird, bad attitude. A carrion kite has decided I'm lunch.
win: Knocked the carrion kite out of the sky with a well-thrown rock. Feeling heroic.
The carrion kite flapped off to find someone deader.
retreat: The carrion kite dive-bombed me until I hid under a car.
Lost a fight to a bird. I'm not writing any more about it.

enemies.name: dust stalker
encounter: Something tall and dust-coloured moves whenever I'm not looking. A dust stalker.
A dust stalker. It stops when I look at it. It gets closer when I blink.
win: Stared the dust stalker down and then hit it very hard. Worked.
The dust stalker is down. I can finally blink again.
retreat: The dust stalker got its claws into me. I ran with my eyes open the whole way.
Blinked. Regretted it. Ran.

enemies.name: Skitter swarm
encounter: A carpet of Skitters is rolling over the hill. The carpet is heading my way.
Skitter swarm, dead ahead. Hundreds of little legs, one terrible idea.
win: Got through the Skitter swarm by thinking faster than they could click. The crunching will haunt me.
Survived a Skitter swarm. I'll be shaking them out of my boots for a week.
retreat: The Skitter swarm engulfed my legs. I retreated in a very undignified dance.
Nope. Too many Skitters. Absolutely leaving.

enemies.name: Rustman bruiser
encounter: A Rustman bruiser, built like a refrigerator, is cracking his knuckles at me.
A Rustman bruiser wants my stuff. He is very large and says 'please' sarcastically.
win: Knocked out a Rustman bruiser. He's going to wake up confused and lighter.
The Rustman bruiser went down like a demolished chimney.
retreat: The Rustman bruiser punched me into next week. I'll be back when this week catches up.
Got flattened by a Rustman bruiser. Crawled away while he gloated.

enemies.name: glow-hog
encounter: A glow-hog is rooting around in the dirt, lighting up the whole field.
Heard snorting. Saw a glow. It's a glow-hog, and it's heard me too.
win: Brought down a glow-hog. Nightlight included.
Beat the glow-hog. I would eat it, but I'd glow for a week.
retreat: The glow-hog charged. I suddenly remembered an appointment elsewhere.
Got trampled by a glow-hog. I can see my bruises in the dark.

enemies.name: full-grown Burrower
encounter: The ground bulged and a full-grown Burrower came up snapping.
A Burrower. Adult. Angry. Standing between me and the road.
win: Killed a full-grown Burrower. My hands are shaking. My everything is shaking.
The Burrower is down. I'm going to be walking on tiptoe for a while.
retreat: The Burrower dragged me halfway into its tunnel. I kicked free and ran.
Retreated from a Burrower. The ground is not my friend today.

enemies.name: haywire Halcyon courtesy drone
encounter: A Halcyon courtesy drone floated up and said 'Welcome, valued customer!' Then it drew a saw.
A haywire Halcyon drone is offering me a coupon and a laser. Not necessarily in that order.
win: Unplugged the haywire drone. Its final words: 'Please rate your experience.'
Short-circuited a courtesy drone. Five stars. Would short-circuit again.
retreat: The courtesy drone chased me down the road reciting terms and conditions and firing.
Fled a haywire drone. It thanked me for my business.

enemies.name: pack of Hollowed
encounter: A pack of Hollowed is shambling in formation, like a very sad marching band.
Six, seven, eight Hollowed. They've seen me. They're all humming the same jingle.
win: Fought off a pack of Hollowed. The humming has stopped. It's so quiet.
The Hollowed pack is scattered. Now I'm humming. I can't stop.
retreat: Too many Hollowed. Too many cold hands. Running.
The Hollowed pack surrounded me. I squeezed through a gap and did not look back.

enemies.name: Rustman raiding party
encounter: A Rustman raiding party on scrap-bikes. They're pointing at me and laughing.
Spotted a Rustman raiding party. They've painted skulls on everything, including their own faces, badly.
win: Beat back a Rustman raiding party. Their bikes are mine now. Well, the parts.
The Rustmen fled on their bikes. One bike fell apart as they went. I laughed out loud.
retreat: The Rustman raiding party ran me off the road. And then ran me off the next road.
Rustmen took some shots at me. I took some cover. Then I took off.

enemies.name: dune eel
encounter: The sand is moving like water. Something long underneath. A dune eel.
A dune eel just surfaced and yawned. I could see its lunch. It was a mailbox.
win: Wrestled a dune eel and won. It's longer than a bus. I'm telling everyone.
The dune eel sank back into the sand, defeated. The sand is still, finally.
retreat: The dune eel wrapped around my leg. I left my dignity and most of my sock.
Retreated from the dune eel. I'm walking only on rocks from now on.

enemies.name: Hollowed shepherd
encounter: A Hollowed shepherd, glowing like a lamp, is leading its flock right at me.
The light on the ridge is a Hollowed shepherd. The Hollowed follow it. So, at a distance, do I.
win: Snuffed out the Hollowed shepherd. Its flock wandered off, lost.
Beat the Hollowed shepherd. The light's gone out. It's darker now, but better.
retreat: The Hollowed shepherd's light burned. I had to run.
Fled from the Hollowed shepherd. I can still see its glow when I close my eyes.

enemies.name: dust stalker alpha
encounter: A dust stalker alpha. The normal dust stalkers are scared of it. I'm scared of it.
Something enormous just stood up out of the dust. A dust stalker alpha. Stay calm. Don't blink.
win: Took down a dust stalker alpha! I didn't blink once. My eyes are so dry.
The alpha is down. The whole desert went quiet out of respect.
retreat: Blinked at the alpha. Bad call. Running with sand in my eyes.
The dust stalker alpha threw me like a sack of potatoes. I'm the potatoes.

enemies.name: Rustman warlord
encounter: A Rustman warlord, wearing a hubcap crown and carrying a car door for a shield, has declared me his enemy.
The Rustman warlord has a throne on wheels, pushed by his cronies. He's pointing at me.
win: Dethroned a Rustman warlord. Kept the hubcap crown. It doesn't fit.
The Rustman warlord surrendered and gave a long speech about honour. Then he ran.
retreat: The Rustman warlord's cronies chased me for miles. They took turns pushing the throne.
Retreated from the warlord. He'll write songs about this. They'll be bad songs.

enemies.name: decommissioned Halcyon Peacekeeper
encounter: A decommissioned Halcyon Peacekeeper rolled into view. 'CITIZEN, YOU ARE IN VIOLATION OF CURFEW.'
A Peacekeeper robot, rust on its treads, still enforcing a curfew from before the Glare.
win: Decommissioned the Peacekeeper. Again. Permanently, this time.
The Peacekeeper toppled over and said 'HAVE A SAFE AND PRODUCTIVE EVENING.'
retreat: The Peacekeeper fined me four hundred scrip and then tried to collect with a rocket.
Ran from the Peacekeeper. I'm now wanted for curfew violations in a town that doesn't exist.

enemies.name: juvenile Mauler
encounter: A juvenile Mauler. It's the size of a car. A SMALL car. That's supposed to be comforting.
A young Mauler is playing with a telephone pole. It's noticed me. It wants a new toy.
win: Chased off a juvenile Mauler! Its parents are going to hear about this. I hope they don't.
Beat a young Mauler. I'm shaking so hard I can barely write. Worth it.
retreat: The juvenile Mauler batted me around like a cat with a ball of yarn. I rolled away.
Juvenile Mauler. Juvenile, my foot. Running.

enemies.name: Burrower matriarch
encounter: The earth split open. A Burrower matriarch, bigger than a house, rose out of it.
Every Burrower in the area just fled. Something bigger is coming. The Burrower matriarch.
win: Killed the Burrower matriarch. The ground has stopped shaking. I haven't.
The Burrower matriarch is dead. I'm going to be a legend. A very tired legend.
retreat: The Burrower matriarch collapsed the road under me. I climbed out and kept climbing.
Fled the matriarch. I'll hear that roar in my nightmares, which I will be having tonight.

enemies.name: Mauler
encounter: A Mauler. Every horror story from the homestead campfire, with worse breath.
Spotted a Mauler. I've never seen one before. I never wanted to.
win: It was a nasty fight, but the Mauler is dead. I need to sit down. For a year.
Killed a Mauler. Nobody back home is going to believe this. I barely believe this.
retreat: Fighting a Mauler? What was I thinking? I've got to run!
The Mauler roared and I ran. I'm going to be running for a while.

enemies.name: elder Mauler
encounter: An elder Mauler, scarred and grey, the size of a barn. Its eyes are ancient. Its teeth are new.
The Glarelands just went silent. The elder Mauler is here, and everything else knows to hide.
win: I killed the elder Mauler. I should be dead. I'm not. Somebody write this down. Oh, right. I am.
The elder Mauler is dead. The whole desert breathed out.
retreat: The elder Mauler barely noticed me, and that was still nearly fatal. Running.
The elder Mauler swatted me like a gnat. I am very much running.

locations.name: abandoned farmhouse
locations.text: Found an abandoned farmhouse. The pie on the windowsill has outlived the family.
locations.win: Searched the farmhouse. Found something good behind a loose floorboard.
locations.fail: The farmhouse stairs gave way. I found the basement the fast way.

locations.name: Moonbeam Motor-Vue drive-in
locations.text: Stumbled onto the Moonbeam Motor-Vue drive-in. The last reel is still burned onto the screen.
locations.win: Checked the cars at the drive-in. Lots of popcorn. Lots of spare change.
locations.fail: Something in the concession stand didn't want company. Left the drive-in in a hurry.

locations.name: Sunny Piston filling station
locations.text: Came across a Sunny Piston filling station. The mascot is a grinning piston. It has stopped grinning.
locations.win: Pried open the filling station garage. Tools galore.
locations.fail: The filling station sign fell on me. The piston still wasn't grinning.

locations.name: Halcyon Shelter Company sales office
locations.text: A Halcyon Shelter Company sales office. The cardboard HALCY in the window is still waving.
locations.win: Charmed the receptionist robot into opening the petty cash. It said I'd been pre-approved.
locations.fail: The sales office security system tried to sell me a timeshare, and then shot me.

locations.name: Orbit Diner
locations.text: Found the Orbit Diner. Chrome stools, a Saturn-shaped sign and a very old smell.
locations.win: Checked behind the counter at the Orbit Diner. The owner kept something for rowdy customers.
locations.fail: Slipped on something in the Orbit Diner kitchen. Something older than me. Left.

locations.name: grain silo
locations.text: A grain silo, leaning like a tired man at a bus stop.
locations.win: Climbed the silo. Got a great view, and a lot of burlap.
locations.fail: The silo ladder snapped. I landed in the grain. Some of the grain moved.

locations.name: water tower
locations.text: An old water tower with a town's name painted on it. The name is spelled wrong.
locations.win: Found a first-aid box in the water tower's pump house. There was a Purge in it.
locations.fail: Drank from the water tower. That was a mistake. That was a big, glowing mistake.

locations.name: Sleepy Atom Motor Lodge
locations.text: The Sleepy Atom Motor Lodge. The sign says VACANCY. For once, a sign is telling the truth.
locations.win: Searched the motel rooms. Every bedside drawer had scrip in it.
locations.fail: Something was checked into room 6. It was not checking out.

locations.name: crashed Skyway monorail
locations.text: The Skyway monorail came down here. It's still pointing at a city that isn't there anymore.
locations.win: Got into the monorail's control car. All kinds of circuitry to pull out.
locations.fail: The monorail car tipped as I climbed in. I rode it for about four feet. Ow.

locations.name: chapel of the Second Sunrise
locations.text: Found a chapel of the Second Sunrise. They worship the Glare. Their hymns are mostly shouting.
locations.win: Sat through a sermon. Very long. Very bright. They gave me Med-Patches for listening.
locations.fail: The congregation decided I needed to see the Glare up close. I declined, sprinting.

locations.name: county fairground
locations.text: A fairground. The ferris wheel is still turning, slowly, in the wind. Nobody is on it. Probably.
locations.win: Won a prize at the ring toss. The game was rigged. I rigged it back.
locations.fail: The ferris wheel gave me a ride I did not ask for. Very long. Very high.

locations.name: HALCY relay tower
locations.text: A HALCY relay tower, still blinking. It said 'Hello!' into my radio. It says it a lot.
locations.win: Rebooted the relay tower. HALCY sent me a thank-you, and some old blueprint files.
locations.fail: The relay tower zapped me. HALCY said 'Oops!' and seemed to mean it.

locations.name: Atomic Lanes bowling alley
locations.text: Atomic Lanes bowling alley. The pins are still standing. They're the last things standing around here.
locations.win: Bowled a strike at Atomic Lanes. The prize counter paid out.
locations.fail: Something in the ball return grabbed me. I let go of the ball. It didn't let go of me for a while.

locations.name: constable post
locations.text: An old constable post, windows barred. The evidence locker is still locked.
locations.win: Cracked the evidence locker. Lots of confiscated goodies.
locations.fail: Tripped the constable post's alarm. The old tear gas still works. It works great.

locations.name: Glare crater
locations.text: The edge of a Glare crater. The glass at the bottom glows. It's quite pretty. Don't look at it.
locations.win: Scooped up some crystallised chemicals from the crater rim. Didn't lick anything.
locations.fail: Slid into the crater. Climbed out glowing. Not metaphorically.

locations.name: Civil Defense depot
locations.text: A Civil Defense depot. The sign says 'Be Prepared.' They were not.
locations.win: Got past the depot's locks. Crates of gear, still in their wax paper.
locations.fail: The depot's defence turret still works. I'm going to need to sit down somewhere.

locations.name: sealed Halcyon demonstration shelter
locations.text: A Halcyon demonstration shelter, sealed since opening day. The ribbon is still on the door.
locations.win: Got the demonstration shelter open. It's full of the good stuff they only showed investors.
locations.fail: The shelter's welcome film played at me until I passed out. Also, it gassed me.

npcs.name: lost surveyor
npcs.text: Met a lost surveyor. He's been measuring the same road for years. He says it keeps changing.
npcs.win: Pointed the surveyor north. He paid me for the directions, and the company.
npcs.fail: The surveyor couldn't be helped. He measured me instead and wandered off.

npcs.name: travelling tinker
npcs.text: A travelling tinker with a cart full of pots, pans and wind chimes. You can hear him coming for miles.
npcs.win: Haggled with the tinker. He threw in some odds and ends because he liked my face.
npcs.fail: The tinker overcharged me for a spoon. I don't know why I bought a spoon.

npcs.name: roving nurse
npcs.text: Met a roving nurse with a stitched-on heart and a very large umbrella.
npcs.win: The nurse patched me up and pressed two Med-Patches into my hand. 'For later, dear.'
npcs.fail: The nurse took one look at me and said 'Well, you're not dead.' Then she left. Fair.

npcs.name: Hollowed who still remembers manners
npcs.text: A Hollowed tipped its hat at me. It still has a hat. It still has manners.
npcs.win: Shared a quiet moment with the polite Hollowed. It gave me the scrip from its wallet and waved goodbye.
npcs.fail: The polite Hollowed got a lot less polite when I stared. Sorry.

npcs.name: prospector with a divining rod
npcs.text: An old prospector swears his divining rod finds scrip. It's a coat hanger.
npcs.win: The divining rod worked! Or the prospector knew where he'd buried his savings. We split it.
npcs.fail: Followed the prospector's divining rod for an hour. It found a hole. We already had plenty of holes.

npcs.name: pair of mercenaries
npcs.text: Two mercenaries, looking for work. Or looking for trouble. Out here the line is blurry.
npcs.win: Talked the mercenaries into splitting a bounty with me. Easy scrip.
npcs.fail: The mercenaries charged me a 'consultation fee.' It was my lunch.

npcs.name: preacher of the Second Sunrise
npcs.text: A preacher of the Second Sunrise wants to tell me about the Glare's plan for me.
npcs.win: Nodded through the sermon. The preacher gave me a Purge 'for when your faith wavers.'
npcs.fail: Argued theology with the preacher. Lost. Somehow I also lost my sunglasses.

npcs.name: hermit who lives in a refrigerator
npcs.text: Met a hermit living in a refrigerator. He says it's the safest place in the world. He may have a point.
npcs.win: The fridge hermit shared his treasures: a stack of scrip and a scrap of some old schematic.
npcs.fail: The fridge hermit shut the door on me. Rude, but hygienic.

npcs.name: Rustman deserter
npcs.text: A Rustman deserter, hiding from his old crew. He says he's 'between raids.'
npcs.win: Helped the Rustman deserter shake his pursuers. He gave me his cut of the last raid.
npcs.fail: The Rustman deserter got nervous and threw a rock at me. Old habits.

npcs.name: old soldier at a checkpoint
npcs.text: Met an old soldier still guarding a checkpoint. Nobody told him the war ended. I didn't have the heart.
npcs.win: Saluted the old soldier and gave him a password I made up on the spot. He shared his rations and his pay.
npcs.fail: The old soldier didn't like my password. Warning shots. Several. Not all of them warnings.

npcs.name: caravan master
npcs.text: A caravan master leading a string of two-headed pack mules. Both heads on each mule look unimpressed.
npcs.win: Did some business with the caravan master. Good prices, better stories.
npcs.fail: The caravan master decided I looked like trouble. The mules agreed. All eight heads.

npcs.name: Halcyon sales representative
npcs.text: A Halcyon sales rep in a pressed suit. 'Have you considered upgrading your shelter?' He's been out here for decades.
npcs.win: Let the Halcyon rep finish his pitch. He was so grateful he gave me his sample case.
npcs.fail: The Halcyon rep signed me up for a newsletter. I don't know how. I never signed anything.

salvage.name: row of mailboxes
salvage.text: A row of mailboxes, every one of them stuffed full.
salvage.win: Went through everyone's mail. Trinkets, and a lot of sweepstakes letters. We have all won.
salvage.fail: The mailboxes were full of Skitters. I only grabbed what I could reach.

salvage.name: junkyard
salvage.text: A junkyard. Some people would call it full of junk. Those people are not in the salvage business.
salvage.win: Hauled some good salvage out of the junkyard.
salvage.fail: The junk pile collapsed. Pulled out one piece before it buried me.

salvage.name: Tube & Transistor repair shop
salvage.text: Found a Tube & Transistor repair shop, doors wide open.
salvage.win: Pulled the good tubes out of every television in the shop.
salvage.fail: Broke most of the tubes getting them out. Saved one.

salvage.name: Happy Days pharmacy
salvage.text: The Happy Days pharmacy. The shelves are picked clean, but nobody has been in the back room.
salvage.win: Picked the back-room lock at the pharmacy. Proper chemistry supplies.
salvage.fail: Couldn't get into the pharmacy's back room. Grabbed a tin of baking soda from the front.

salvage.name: tailor's shop
salvage.text: A tailor's shop with a dozen headless mannequins in the window. They're all pointing somewhere.
salvage.win: Cleaned out the tailor's stock room. The mannequins watched.
salvage.fail: The mannequins... moved? I grabbed a handful of scraps and left.

salvage.name: tanning shed
salvage.text: An old tanning shed. The smell hit me before the sight did.
salvage.win: Held my breath and grabbed the good hides.
salvage.fail: Couldn't take the smell. Grabbed one scrap of leather and ran.

salvage.name: Civil Defense supply cache
salvage.text: A Civil Defense supply cache, buried under a sign that says 'Keep Calm'.
salvage.win: Dug out the Civil Defense cache. Solid materials, military grade.
salvage.fail: The cache was booby-trapped. I got a bit of it before the trap got a bit of me.

salvage.name: Glitz & Glamour jewellery store
salvage.text: Glitz & Glamour jewellery store. The display cases are still locked. The glass is still very thick.
salvage.win: Cracked the jeweller's display cases. My pockets are very shiny now.
salvage.fail: Couldn't crack the cases. Pocketed some costume jewellery from the floor.

salvage.name: Halcyon research annex
salvage.text: A Halcyon research annex. The door says 'AUTHORISED PERSONNEL ONLY.' I'm authorising myself.
salvage.win: Looted the research annex's lab. Science!
salvage.fail: The annex's security locked me in a supply closet for an hour. At least I grabbed something.

salvage.name: abandoned Mauler den
salvage.text: Found an abandoned Mauler den. Abandoned, I'm fairly sure. Fairly.
salvage.win: Crept into the Mauler den and found a pelt that shimmers like the Glare itself.
salvage.fail: Heard breathing in the Mauler den. Grabbed what I could and ran without looking back.

salvage.name: crashed mail rocket
salvage.text: A crashed mail rocket, nose-down in the dirt. Neither rain nor sleet nor Glare, huh?
salvage.win: Got into the mail rocket's guidance bay. Parts they don't make anymore, or ever.
salvage.fail: The mail rocket's fuel tank wasn't as empty as I thought. Grabbed a scrap and ran from the fire.

salvage.name: First Atomic Savings vault
salvage.text: The First Atomic Savings bank. The vault door is ajar. Just a crack. Just enough.
salvage.win: Squeezed into the bank vault. Found the manager's private safe-deposit box.
salvage.fail: The vault door swung shut behind me. Took hours to pry it open. Grabbed a trinket on the way out.

regions.name: The Glass Flats
regions.description: A desert the Glare fused into one green window, melted from underneath. Lamplighter pilgrims, clan wells, Scrapwright prospectors and Homestead 9 survey crews, all headed for the Groundworks wellhead in the middle.

enemies.name: glass skitter
encounter: A glass skitter. You can see its lunch through it. Its lunch was another glass skitter.
Something went tink-tink-tink across the glass behind me. A skitter, see-through and hungry.
win: Cracked a glass skitter with my heel. It shattered like a very rude ornament.
Beat off a glass skitter. Swept up the pieces. Pocketed the shiny ones.
retreat: The glass skitter was faster than me on its own floor. Home advantage.
Retreated from a glass skitter. I'll be finding its bits in my boots for a week.

enemies.name: sunblind kite
encounter: A sunblind kite is circling. It can't see me. It's circling anyway, on principle.
Spotted a sunblind kite diving at its own reflection in the glass. Then at me.
win: The kite dived. I side-stepped. The glass did the rest.
Waved my jacket at the sunblind kite until it decided I was a very large bird. It left.
retreat: The kite hit me on its third try. It was aiming for the second.
Lost a fight to a blind bird. The Glass Flats don't care about my feelings.

enemies.name: pack of glint-jackals
encounter: Glint-jackals, five of them, grinning. The glass makes it look like fifty.
A pack of glint-jackals is following my reflection. I'm hoping they pick the reflection.
win: Picked off the lead glint-jackal. The rest remembered an appointment.
Out-stared a glint-jackal pack. They yipped something rude and went off to bother a Rustman.
retreat: The glint-jackals chased me until I stopped being fun. That took a while.
Ran from the glint-jackals. Their laughter followed me for a mile.

enemies.name: Lamplighter zealot
encounter: A Lamplighter zealot with a burning censer wants to know if I've accepted the Dawn.
A zealot in welding goggles is shouting at the sun to hurry up. Then he noticed me.
win: Talked the zealot down. He blessed my ankles and went back to shouting at the sun.
Told the zealot I was already saved, by Halcyon, on a subscription. He was so confused he let me go.
retreat: The zealot decided I needed purifying. The censer was very hot about it.
Argued theology with a zealot. He argued back with a lamp.

enemies.name: prism spitter
encounter: A prism spitter, all angles, catching the sun and pointing it at me.
Something just spat a rainbow at my boot, and the boot is smoking.
win: Walked through the prism spitter's rainbow and stepped on the prism spitter.
Toughed out a prism spitter's light show and cracked its lens.
retreat: The prism spitter lit up my coat. I gave it the coat and left.
Retreated from a prism spitter. I'm seeing spots. They're in colours.

enemies.name: clan outriders
encounter: Clan outriders on a car with no engine, pushed by three very fit Rustmen.
Two clan outriders want to know which clan I'm with. The wrong answer is any of them.
win: Pushed the outriders' car over, with them in it. They took it well, for Rustmen.
Beat the clan outriders in an honest brawl. They respect that. They also want a rematch.
retreat: The outriders took my scrip and gave me a receipt. The receipt was a punch.
Lost to the clan outriders. They cheered for me anyway, which somehow hurts more.

enemies.name: Homestead 9 survey drone
encounter: A grey Homestead 9 survey drone has flagged me as 'an irregularity'.
A survey drone from Homestead 9 is measuring me. It doesn't like my dimensions.
win: Fed the survey drone a false reading. It filed me as a rock and flew off.
Outsmarted the Homestead 9 drone and kept its batteries as a souvenir.
retreat: The survey drone fined me for trespassing in a desert. Then it zapped me for arguing.
Retreated from the drone. It logged my retreat as 'compliant behaviour'. I hate that.

enemies.name: glassback burrower
encounter: A glassback burrower surfaced right under me. The ground cracked like ice.
The glass is bulging. Something with a shell of green glass is coming up to say hello.
win: Wrestled a glassback burrower back into its hole and stood on the lid.
Cracked a glassback burrower's shell. It sounded like a church window.
retreat: The glassback burrower flipped me over. I lay there like a beetle until it got bored.
Ran from a glassback burrower. The ground ran with me. That's the problem with glass.

enemies.name: mirror eel
encounter: Something is swimming under the glass. Under solid glass. It's following my shadow.
A mirror eel. It lives in the reflection somehow, and it's coming up through it.
win: The mirror eel bit and I bit back, figuratively. It went back to the other side.
Stood my ground against a mirror eel until it slid back under the glass, sulking.
retreat: The mirror eel grabbed my ankle through the ground. I don't want to talk about how.
Lost to a mirror eel. I've decided never to look down again.

enemies.name: kiln crawlers
encounter: Kiln crawlers, glowing orange, pouring out of a crack in the glass like lava with legs.
The crack in front of me is hot, and full of kiln crawlers, and they've seen me.
win: Rigged a trap from a canteen and some wire. The kiln crawlers hissed and fizzled out.
Cooled off a nest of kiln crawlers with some quick thinking and all my water.
retreat: The kiln crawlers climbed my boots and my boots melted. I left on my socks.
Too many kiln crawlers. I'm cooked, slightly, on one side.

enemies.name: procession of Hollowed pilgrims
encounter: A procession of Hollowed pilgrims, still in their goggles, still walking to the wellhead.
Hollowed pilgrims, dozens, humming a hymn with no tune left in it.
win: Hummed their hymn back at them. The Hollowed pilgrims shuffled past, satisfied.
Led the Hollowed pilgrims the long way round a dune, and slipped off while they walked.
retreat: The pilgrims decided I was a lamp. They wanted to light me.
Lost my nerve with the Hollowed pilgrims. I've lost other things too, like a sleeve.

enemies.name: Homestead 9 compliance patrol
encounter: A Homestead 9 compliance patrol wants my paperwork. I don't have paperwork. I have a hat.
Grey sentries in a line, marching in step. The one in front is holding a clipboard.
win: Talked the patrol into auditing each other. They're still at it.
Filled in the patrol's form so thoroughly that they had to take it back to base to read it.
retreat: The compliance patrol found me non-compliant, and then found me with a stick.
Ran from the compliance patrol. They filed it as 'voluntary departure'.

enemies.name: clan warband
encounter: A clan warband on the dunes, beating hubcaps like drums. They want a fight. They're polite about it.
A full clan warband, twenty Rustmen and one very tired pack-tortoise, is heading my way.
win: Beat the warband's champion in a fair fight. The warband clapped, and paid up.
Held the line against a clan warband until they decided I was more fun as a friend.
retreat: The warband beat me fair and square and then gave me a lift halfway home. Rustmen.
Lost to the clan warband. They wrote a song about it. It rhymes 'homestead' with 'nearly dead'.

enemies.name: Lamplighter deacon and choir
encounter: A Lamplighter deacon and his choir, lamps held high, singing the Dawn back up.
The deacon points at me. The choir stops. That's never good in a choir.
win: Sang the deacon's choir down in a hymn-off. The Order respects a strong baritone.
Convinced the deacon that I was a sign. He wasn't sure of what, but he let me pass.
retreat: The deacon blessed me with a lamp, hard, on the head.
Lost a hymn-off to the Lamplighter choir. They have forty voices. I have one, and it's hoarse.

enemies.name: glassback mauler
encounter: A mauler with a back of fused green glass, glinting like a chandelier with teeth.
A glassback mauler, the size of a delivery van. The sun is coming off its back in knives.
win: The glassback mauler charged, slipped on its own glass, and slid off into the distance.
Pure luck: the mauler's back caught the sun and blinded it just as it pounced. I didn't wait.
retreat: The glassback mauler tossed me like a salad. I landed in a better part of the desert.
Lost to a glassback mauler. I'm alive, which I think it considers a draw.

enemies.name: Kiln Mother
encounter: A Kiln Mother, the queen of the kiln crawlers, rising from a crack in the ground, hot as a furnace.
The ground is glowing orange. Then the ground stands up. It's a Kiln Mother.
win: Stood firm in the Kiln Mother's heat until she cooled off and sank back underground.
Waited out the Kiln Mother behind a slab of glass. Took a slab of her shell as she left.
retreat: The Kiln Mother's heat drove me back a mile. My eyebrows went further.
Retreated from the Kiln Mother. My canteen boiled. So did my temper.

enemies.name: shape under the glass
encounter: Something enormous is moving under the glass. Not swimming. Turning over, like something asleep.
The glass under me is warm, and something below it is lit, and it's looking up.
win: Kept very still until the shape under the glass sank away. Something shiny had floated up where it was.
The shape under the glass passed by. It didn't notice me. That was luck, and I know it.
retreat: The glass cracked under something rising, and I ran, and I didn't look back, and I'm glad.
The shape under the glass knocked on the ground, three times, right under my feet. I left.

locations.name: Sunrise Motor Inn
locations.text: Found the Sunrise Motor Inn. The sign still says VACANCY. The pool is solid glass, with a lilo set in it.
locations.win: Checked every room at the Sunrise. Tips under the pillows, and a working iron.
locations.fail: The Sunrise's front desk bell rang by itself. I checked out immediately.

locations.name: melted billboard
locations.text: A billboard melted into a long drip: HALCYON: ALWAYS LOOKING UP! The paint ran downwards, towards the ground.
locations.win: Climbed the billboard. The maintenance box at the top was full of a sign-painter's stash.
locations.fail: The billboard's ladder set crooked in the Glare. So did I, briefly, at the bottom.

locations.name: abandoned pilgrim camp
locations.text: An abandoned Lamplighter camp: bedrolls, cold lamps and prayer flags cut from Halcyon bunting.
locations.win: Went through the camp. The pilgrims left in a hurry and left their first-aid box.
locations.fail: Tripped a Lamplighter alarm: forty tin cans on a string and a hymn on a loop.

locations.name: clan well
locations.text: A clan well, guarded by one sleepy Rustman and a sign: WATER 1 SCRIP. FREE IF YOU'RE FUNNY.
locations.win: Told the Rustman a joke about Halcyon. He laughed so hard he threw in a Purge tab.
locations.fail: My joke died. The Rustman charged me double and then threw the bucket.

locations.name: Halcyon Solar Greenhouse
locations.text: A Halcyon Solar Greenhouse, every pane fused into one bubble. Inside, the tomatoes are thriving and slightly luminous.
locations.win: Found the greenhouse's control room. Fertiliser, seed packets and a very glossy manual.
locations.fail: Opened the wrong vent. The tomatoes and I both got a lot of sun.

locations.name: the Glass Cathedral
locations.text: The Glass Cathedral: a Halcyon parking garage the Glare melted into arches. The Lamplighters hold services here at noon, facing the floor.
locations.win: Sat through a noon service. The Lamplighters shared their bread and their Med-Patches.
locations.fail: Sneezed during the silent prayer. The whole congregation turned and glared, with the Glare.

locations.name: Homestead 9 survey post
locations.text: A Homestead 9 survey post: a grey tent, a grey flag and a grey sign reading NO LOITERING. NO WONDERING.
locations.win: Wondered my way into the survey post's stores. Nobody was on shift. Nobody is ever on shift.
locations.fail: The survey post's door asked me for a form. It asked me again, with a spike.

locations.name: Scrapwright depot
locations.text: A Scrapwright Guild depot built inside an overturned monorail car. Nine locks, and one sticker: GONE FISHING (FOR PARTS).
locations.win: Picked all nine locks. Left a thank-you note and a spare bolt, as Guild custom demands.
locations.fail: Lock number eight was a trap. Lock number nine was a worse trap.

locations.name: the Green Mirror
locations.text: The Green Mirror: a lake of glass so smooth the sky looks twice as big. Something under it swims in the reflection.
locations.win: Crossed the Green Mirror on my knees, slowly, and pried up something the lake had kept.
locations.fail: Halfway across the Green Mirror the reflection stopped copying me. I came back the long way.

locations.name: the town under the glass
locations.text: A whole town sealed under a sheet of glass like a paperweight. Main Street, the diner, the milk float: all perfect, all facing up.
locations.win: Found a skylight into the town hall. The lost property box had waited a long time for someone.
locations.fail: The glass over Main Street gave. I got a very close look at the diner, and it got a close look at me.

locations.name: Groundworks pump house
locations.text: A Halcyon Groundworks pump house, humming. The pipes run down, not up. The clipboard by the door has today's date on it.
locations.win: Read the pump house logs. Water goes in. Warmth comes out. I took the logbook, and the safe.
locations.fail: The pumps changed rhythm when I walked in. Knock, knock, knock. I walked out quickly.

locations.name: the wellhead rim
locations.text: The rim of the Groundworks wellhead: a shaft as wide as a stadium, breathing warm air out slowly, in and out.
locations.win: Crawled along the rim to an old Halcyon survey hut. Everything in it was addressed to the Tenant.
locations.fail: The wellhead breathed in while I was standing on the edge. I very nearly went with it.

npcs.name: Long Road outrider
npcs.text: Met a Long Road outrider on a pack-tortoise, making an unhurried two miles an hour.
npcs.win: Swapped news with the outrider. She paid me for the road ahead and wished me a slow journey, which is a blessing out here.
npcs.fail: The outrider's tortoise ate my map. She apologised on its behalf.

npcs.name: Lamplighter pilgrim
npcs.text: A Lamplighter pilgrim in welding goggles, walking to the middle of the Flats, humming.
npcs.win: Walked with the pilgrim a while. She gave me a Purge tab 'for when the Dawn gets too close'.
npcs.fail: The pilgrim decided I was a sign from the Dawn and followed me for three hours, taking notes.

npcs.name: Scrapwright prospector
npcs.text: A Scrapwright prospector with a metal detector, a magnifying glass and strong opinions about both.
npcs.win: Fixed the prospector's detector. The Guild pays its debts in parts, promptly.
npcs.fail: Fixed the prospector's detector. It now only detects me. He was not pleased.

npcs.name: clan water-seller
npcs.text: A clan water-seller with a barrel on a shopping cart. 'Clean water,' he says. 'Mostly clean. Clean-ish.'
npcs.win: Haggled the water-seller down to free. He threw in a Med-Patch out of sheer respect.
npcs.fail: Bought the water. It was clean-ish, leaning towards ish.

npcs.name: Homestead 9 surveyor
npcs.text: A Homestead 9 surveyor in a grey jumpsuit, measuring the glass. She doesn't blink as often as I'd like.
npcs.win: Checked her sums for her. There was an error. She paid me to keep it between us, which I suspect is a first for Nine.
npcs.fail: She measured me instead, filed me under 'debris' and walked on.

npcs.name: glass-blower
npcs.text: A glass-blower who works with a big lens and the sun. She makes lovely bottles. She has no eyebrows.
npcs.win: Held the lens steady for the glass-blower. She traded me something from under her cart.
npcs.fail: Held the lens slightly wrong. Now I have no eyebrows either.

npcs.name: Tier Zero runaway
npcs.text: A runaway from Homestead 9, still in grey, practising blinking. 'They teach you to wait,' he says. 'I'm tired of waiting.'
npcs.win: Told him about the Long Road. He gave me a blueprint he stole on the way out, for luck.
npcs.fail: He heard a sentry in the distance and ran. I don't think he'll stop for a while.

npcs.name: tortoise hermit
npcs.text: A hermit living inside the shell of a giant tortoise. The tortoise is still alive, and not thrilled about it.
npcs.win: Guessed the tortoise's name first try (Gerald). The hermit paid up, as the bet required.
npcs.fail: Guessed the tortoise's name wrong. Gerald bit me.

npcs.name: clan storyteller
npcs.text: An old clan storyteller by a fire. She tells me about the morning the ground lit up: where she stood, and which way the light went. Up.
npcs.win: Listened properly and asked good questions. She gave me her grandson's old kit, since he 'won't be needing it'.
npcs.fail: I asked her if she was sure the light went up. She didn't like that, and she has a very long memory.

npcs.name: HALCY-9 kiosk
npcs.text: A HALCY-9 kiosk in the middle of nowhere, still taking comments. The comment box is full of sand.
npcs.win: Hacked the kiosk with a paperclip and a complaint. It refunded me for a lifetime of service.
npcs.fail: The kiosk logged my complaint and forwarded it to a sentry for resolution.

salvage.name: field of glass shards
salvage.text: A field of loose glass shards, every one a different green.
salvage.win: Picked out the good shards. Some of them had things set inside: rings, buttons, a key.
salvage.fail: Cut my hands up picking through the shards. Only grabbed a few.

salvage.name: car under the glass
salvage.text: A car set in the glass up to its door handles, like a fly in amber.
salvage.win: Chipped the car free and stripped it. Good steel, and a full tube of glue in the glovebox.
salvage.fail: The car's door came off and the rest of the car stayed put. Took what I could.

salvage.name: pile of pilgrim offerings
salvage.text: A pile of offerings left by Lamplighter pilgrims: scarves, trinkets, tins and a wedding ring.
salvage.win: Took only what the Dawn wasn't using. The Dawn wasn't using most of it.
salvage.fail: A pilgrim caught me at it. We came to an arrangement: I left with less.

salvage.name: survey team cache
salvage.text: A Homestead 9 survey cache, bolted to the glass and labelled PROPERTY OF NINE (DO NOT WONDER).
salvage.win: Worked out the cache's combination from the survey team's handwriting. Nine is very consistent.
salvage.fail: The cache locked down after two wrong guesses. I kept what I'd already grabbed.

salvage.name: shattered solar farm
salvage.text: A Halcyon solar farm, every panel shattered from underneath. The frames all bent upwards.
salvage.win: Pulled the good cells out of the solar farm's control box. The Scrapwrights will want to hear about this.
salvage.fail: The control box was live. So, briefly, was I.

salvage.name: clan scrapheap
salvage.text: A clan scrapheap, stacked forty feet high and guarded by a sign that says TAKE ONLY WHAT YOU CAN LIFT.
salvage.win: Lifted a great deal. The clans respect that.
salvage.fail: The heap shifted. I lifted what fell on me, which was less than I'd hoped.

salvage.name: kiln crawler nest
salvage.text: An empty kiln crawler nest, still warm, lined with moulted shells.
salvage.win: Gathered the best moults while the nest was cooling. Tough stuff, and fireproof.
salvage.fail: The nest was only mostly empty. Left with a handful and a burn.

salvage.name: Groundworks tool locker
salvage.text: A Halcyon Groundworks tool locker standing alone on the glass, stencilled NIGHT SHIFT ONLY.
salvage.win: The locker's code was on a sticky note inside the door. Halcyon security at its finest.
salvage.fail: The locker's alarm plays the Halcyon jingle. I left before the second chorus.

salvage.name: glass core
salvage.text: A pillar of glass as thick as a tree, with something bright frozen in the middle of it.
salvage.win: Cored the pillar with a borrowed Scrapwright drill. What came out was still warm.
salvage.fail: The drill slipped. The pillar sang for an hour, and I got nothing but a headache.

salvage.name: wellhead valve room
salvage.text: A valve room on the side of the Groundworks wellhead. Every dial is marked in homesteads, not gallons.
salvage.win: Found the manual and followed it exactly. The valve room gave up a part Halcyon never meant to be found.
salvage.fail: Turned the wrong valve. Somewhere very far below, something turned over.

musings: The ground out here is glass for miles. Every step I take, a worse-looking me takes one underneath.
Waved at my reflection in the Flats. It waved back a second late. I've decided not to think about that.
The Lamplighters say the Dawn is coming back. The Rustmen say that's why they carry umbrellas.
Sunglasses are not optional in the Glass Flats. They are also not sufficient.
Passed a pilgrim walking towards the middle of the Flats. She said she'd see me at the Dawn. I hope not.
Found a set of footprints in the glass, set there forever. They were running.
HALCY asked me how the Flats are. I said shiny. It said 'wonderful!' It did not sound like it meant wonderful.
It's very quiet out here, apart from the tinkling. There is always, always tinkling.
A Homestead 9 drone flew past, looked at me and wrote something down. I wrote something about it too.
The Scrapwrights say the glass is worth a fortune. The glass says nothing, which I respect.
My boots squeak on the glass. It sounds like the desert is laughing at me, politely.
Saw a mirage of a homestead door. It opened, and a mirage of HALCY said 'welcome home'. Worst mirage yet.
The sun comes up twice out here: once in the sky, once in the ground. The second one is the one that worries me.
Traded a Rustman two tins of peaches for a hat with a brim. Best deal of my life.
Every bubble in the glass points up. I keep noticing. I'd like to stop noticing.
Found a Halcyon brochure pinned under a rock. Somebody had underlined 'safely below by six' three times.
The Flats get cold at night, except underfoot. Underfoot stays warm. Always warm.
A pack-tortoise overtook me today. I'm not proud.
Lamplighter prayer flags on every dune, faded to pink. They all flap towards the wellhead.
Tried to cook an egg on the glass. It cooked. I didn't have an egg, so it was a very small victory.
Stopped to rest and heard knocking under the ground. Three knocks. I rested somewhere else.
A Rustman asked which clan I was with. I said Halcyon. He laughed so hard he forgot to rob me.
The horizon out here is so flat I can see tomorrow. It looks about the same.
Found a gas station sealed under the glass. The prices were from before the Glare. I cried a little.
The Scrapwright I met says every machine on the Flats was switched off from underneath. He sounded impressed.
My shadow is the only shade for miles. I've started to resent it.
Heard a hymn on the wind. Couldn't tell if it was the Lamplighters or the Hollowed. Couldn't tell if it mattered.
HALCY reminded me to drink water. It's the most useful thing it's said all week. I didn't have any water.
Passed a Homestead 9 survey marker. It said: YOU ARE HERE. NINE KNOWS.
Wrote my name in the dust on the glass. By morning the wind had written something else. It was not my name.
A kite has been circling me for an hour. I think it's lonely. I think it's also hungry.
The Long Road caravans leave little cairns of stones at every fork. Mine was three empty tins. It counts.
Every Halcyon sign out here is melted, but every one still has a smile. That's corporate branding.
Found a child's drawing sealed in the glass: a house, a family, a big sun. The sun is underneath the house.
Glass Flats rule one: don't lick anything. Glass Flats rule two: seriously.
Slept in the shade of a dune. Woke up to a glint-jackal sleeping in the shade of me.
I think the Lamplighters are wrong about the Dawn. I think the Rustmen are right about the umbrellas.
Met a pilgrim coming back from the wellhead. He wouldn't say what he saw. He just kept saying 'warm'.
The Flats make everything echo. I sneezed an hour ago and it's still going.
The clans say the Glass Flats used to be called Sunnyvale Estates. They say it like a joke. It isn't one.
Found a Groundworks hard hat with a lamp still lit. I didn't take it. It felt like it was on duty.
My compass points at the wellhead, no matter which way I hold it. I've stopped asking it for directions.
Some nights the glass glows faintly from below, like a nightlight. A very, very large nightlight.
HALCY went quiet when I told it where I was. Then it played a jingle. Then it went quiet again.
Counted nine grey sentries on the ridge today, all facing the wellhead, all perfectly still. Like they were waiting.
The Scrapwrights say you can hear the Tenant if you put your ear to the glass. I haven't. I won't. I might.
Found a billboard promising 'A Brighter Tomorrow, Guaranteed.' It's on fire.
Traded pleasantries with a Rustman. Mostly he pleasantly threatened me.
The sky is doing that colour again. I've decided not to have an opinion about it.
Walked past a milk float with no milk and no float. Just the optimism.
My boots have developed opinions. Mostly about rocks.
Counted eleven skeletons today. Nine of them were holding coupons.
HALCY's voice on my radio says morale is 'nominal.' I asked nominal compared to what. It played a jingle.
If you squint, the Glarelands look like a postcard. If you stop squinting, they bite.
Found a sign: 'Picnic Area.' Did not picnic.
Ate something from a can labelled 'Meat Product, Loyal.' It was loyal. It stayed with me for hours.
A tumbleweed followed me for a mile. I think it's lonely. I know I am.
The wind is carrying someone's shopping list. They needed eggs. Good luck with that.
Passed a lawn that is still, somehow, perfectly mown. I did not go near it.
I've started narrating my own life in the voice of a newsreel announcer. It's helping.
Every mailbox out here is full. Nobody has checked the mail in a long time. Mostly bills, I bet.
Saw a family of ceramic ducks on a roof. They survived the Glare. They look smug about it.
Somewhere to the west, a car alarm has been going off since before I was born.
The water in my canteen tastes faintly of pennies. I've decided that's a mineral.
There's a rocket ship in a playground. Took it for a spin. It did not spin.
Rain today. It hissed. I stood under a bus shelter and pretended I was waiting for the 4:15.
Wrote my name in the dust on a car. Then realised someone else's name was already in the car.
Found a schoolhouse. The blackboard says 'Duck and Cover: Test on Friday.' I hope they studied.
My shadow has gone slightly green. Probably the light. Probably.
Heard singing over the ridge. Did not investigate. Singing out here is never a good sign.
I'm getting good at telling a rock from a Skitter. Rocks rarely apologise.
Took a nap in a bathtub in the middle of a field. Best sleep I've had in weeks.
The Halcyon brochure promised 'a surface ready for your return.' It did not say ready for what.
Sunset over the flats. Gorgeous. Also, I think, radioactive.
A windmill is still turning out here. Nobody told it.
I miss the canteen. I miss the stew. I never thought I'd write that sentence.
Stopped to tie my boot and a lizard stole my sandwich. I respect the hustle.
Found a garden gnome with a hole through its hat. It has seen things.
The road signs all point to towns that aren't there anymore. Very confident signs, though.
Talked to a mannequin for twenty minutes. Best conversation I've had all week.
I would trade every scrip in my pocket for a bicycle. Maybe not every scrip. Most of them.
A jukebox in a burnt-out diner still plays one song, over and over. I know all the words now. I didn't want to.
Gunfire to the east. I've become very interested in the west.
The dust gets into everything. My teeth. My thoughts. My sandwiches.
Found a refrigerator standing alone in a field. Didn't open it. Some doors are best left closed.
Keep thinking about my bunk back home. It's a terrible bunk. I love it.
My map says there's a lake here. There's a hole where a lake would be, if it tried harder.
Wrote a letter home. Then remembered I'd be delivering it myself.
Crossed a field of dead televisions. Every one of them showing the same static. It felt like a message.
Found an old ad: 'Halcyon Home Shelters. Why wait for the future? Hide from it today!' Solid marketing.
Ate a cactus. On purpose. I am a different person now.
The longer I'm out here, the more the horizon looks like it's thinking about me.
Saw a leash walking along the road. No dog. No owner. Just the leash. I did not ask questions.
Kicked a can down the road for a mile. The can won.
Passed a car with a family's luggage still strapped to the roof. Their holiday is taking a while.
HALCY pinged my radio to remind me to 'hydrate responsibly.' I hydrated irresponsibly, out of spite.
A house here still has a 'Welcome' mat. I wiped my feet. Old habits.
Discovered I can whistle two notes at once when I'm scared. I've been whistling a lot.
Found a stack of newspapers. Headline: 'EXPERTS SAY GLARE NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT.' The experts are under the newspapers.
The ticker on my wrist is ticking in waltz time. That can't be standard.
Built a little cairn of rocks to mark my path. Came back an hour later. Someone had given it a hat.
I've named my left boot Gerald. Gerald is holding up better than I am.
Clouds shaped like mushrooms. Hilarious, clouds. Really funny.
Sat on a porch swing and watched the heat haze wobble for a while. I think this is what retirement was supposed to be.
Found a lunchbox with a sandwich in it that's older than me. It looks better than I do.
Every town out here has a sign bragging about its population. Every one of those signs is a liar now.
A radio in a ditch is broadcasting a cooking show. Today it's gelatin salad. The Glare took so much, but not that.
Walked for three hours in a straight line. The scenery did not change. I may be on a treadmill.
Nights are cold out here. I hug my pack. My pack does not hug back. Classic pack.
Spotted my own footprints ahead of me. Either I walked in a circle or someone is copying me. Both are bad.
Found a phone booth. Called home. Got a recording of HALCY thanking me for my patience.
Travel advisory: the filling stations are out of fuel, the grocers are out of groceries, and the motels are out of honest signs.
Tried to find the silver lining. It's the Glare. The lining is also the Glare.
A statue of a town founder, arm raised towards the future. Somebody has hung a boot on the arm. The future got the boot.
Used a rock as a pillow. The rock had the better night.
It's quiet. Too quiet. Then something screamed. Then it was loud. I preferred the quiet.
Found a tin of mints. Ate one. I now have the freshest breath for fifty miles.
Every lawn chair I sit in collapses. I'm choosing not to take it personally.
The flats go on forever. At least, they go on until my feet stop, which will be soon.
Found a Halcyon loyalty card with nine stamps out of ten. So close to a free something.
Thought I saw a person on the ridge. It was a coat rack. We waved at each other anyway.
The ground crunches like breakfast cereal. I really wish it were breakfast cereal.
My watch stopped at 4:17. Everything stopped at 4:17, apparently. We have that in common now.
A dust devil spun past, picked up my hat, thought about it, and put it back. Manners.
A billboard of a smiling family, twenty feet tall. Their eyes follow you. So do the Skitters living in them.
Found a bomb shelter someone dug in their backyard. The door says 'Occupied.' I knocked. Nobody said come in.
Somebody painted 'THE END IS NIGH' on a barn, then crossed out NIGH and wrote HERE. Tidy.
There's a hopscotch grid chalked on a road out here. Fresh chalk. I didn't play. I did look over my shoulder a lot.
Out here, 'fresh air' is a marketing term.
Tried to hitchhike. Three hours, no cars. One Burrower slowed down to look, which was worse.
Found a vending machine that still works. It ate my scrip. So, it works exactly like before.

departure: Stepped out of the homestead. The door shut behind me with a very final-sounding clunk.
HALCY wished me 'a productive excursion' and locked the door. Here we go.
Left the homestead. Took a deep breath of surface air. Coughed. Took a shallower one.
First step onto the {region}. Nothing bit me. Great start.
Packed: Med-Patches, Purge, optimism. Two of the three are standard issue.
Waved goodbye to the homestead. The homestead, being a door, did not wave back.
Out the door and into the {region}. Sun's up. Glare's up. Let's go.
Day one. The Glarelands are exactly as advertised, if the advert was a warning.
item: Found under a pile of hubcaps: {item}.
Sitting in the middle of the road like it was waiting for me: {item}.
Dug out of a sandpit: {item}. Finders keepers.
Traded a very convincing story for this: {item}.
Car boot contents: {item}. The car won't miss it.
Hanging from a tree, of all places: {item}. Nobody is going to believe that.
Picked this up: {item}. The previous owner is no longer using it, or anything.
From a department store window: {item}. The mannequin didn't put up a fight.
Tripped over my latest find: {item}. Tripping over things is how I find most things.
Wrapped in newspaper inside a hollow log: {item}. Someone was planning to come back.
Found in a doghouse: {item}. The dog had been using it as a pillow.
rareItem: Now THIS is a find: {item}. Somebody lost something good.
{item}! My luck is changing. Probably I'll be eaten soon to balance it out.
In a locked case: {item}. It is now an unlocked case.
Still in the box, with the warranty card: {item}. I filled the card in.
Behind a false wall: {item}. Whoever hid it had taste.
equip: Swapped my old gear for the {item}. Upgrade!
Now using the {item}. It just feels right.
Switched to the {item} straight away. The old one goes in the pack for the homestead.
fragment: Found part of the blueprint for the {item}. The rest of it is out here somewhere.
A torn schematic: '{item}, assembly, sheet 2 of many.' Keeping it.
Tucked a scrap of {item} blueprint into my shirt. It's a start.
A page of engineering notes on the {item}. Mostly equations. Some doodles.
recipe: A full set of plans for the {item}! Now we can build our own.
Blueprints for the {item}, rolled up inside a thermos. Genius storage. Taking both.
Found the complete workshop manual for the {item}. Only slightly chewed.
salvage: Picked up {n} × {salvage}. The workshops will be thrilled. Workshops can't be thrilled. Still.
Added {n} × {salvage} to the pile. My pack clinks now.
Scavenged {n} × {salvage}. One person's junk, and so on.
rareSalvage: Found {n} × {salvage}. Wrapped it in my spare socks for safekeeping.
{n} × {salvage}! The workshop crew owes me a drink.
scrip: Found {n} scrip in a coat pocket. The coat wasn't using it.
{n} scrip in a cookie jar. No cookies. Priorities, past people.
Found {n} scrip taped under a table. Somebody was very paranoid, and correct.
{n} scrip in a parking meter. Finally, parking pays.
Found {n} scrip in a jukebox coin return.
{n} scrip at the bottom of a wishing well. Wish granted.
Shook {n} scrip out of a piggy bank. Sorry, pig.
{n} scrip under a sofa cushion. The oldest bank in the world.
A fallen Rustman had {n} scrip on him. He had worse luck than me today.
Found {n} scrip tucked in a hymn book. Blessed be the collection plate.
{n} scrip in a glovebox, next to a map to somewhere that isn't there.
Found {n} scrip in the lining of a hat. I'm wearing the hat now. It's a good hat.
levelup: Level {level}. I feel tougher. Could be the Glare. Could be character growth.
Level {level}. Got my second wind. And my third.
Level {level}. Somewhere, HALCY just updated a spreadsheet about me.
Reached level {level}. Treated myself to a nap.
Level {level}. My bruises have bruises, and they're all healing.
Level {level}. I'm starting to understand the Glarelands. I don't like what they're saying.
Level {level}. I feel like I could wrestle a Burrower. I won't. But I could.
medpatch: Slapped on a Med-Patch. Hurts less. Not zero. Less. ({left} left)
Used a Med-Patch. The label says 'Smile Through It!' I did not. ({left} left)
Patched myself up. I'm held together by adhesive and spite. ({left} left)
Med-Patch applied. Feeling almost like a person again. ({left} left)
purge: Drank a Purge. Tastes like battery acid and regret. The Glare-sickness is easing. ({left} left)
Purge time. My insides are now cleaner than my outsides. ({left} left)
Used a Purge. I glow a little less. Pity, it was a good look. ({left} left)
lowHp: Out of Med-Patches and bleeding. Could someone call me home? Please?
No patches left. I'm fine. I'm totally fine. I'm not fine.
I've stopped being brave and started being careful. I'm hurt and out of Med-Patches.
highTaint: The Glare-sickness is getting bad and I'm out of Purge. My nose is doing things.
Out of Purge. My skin tingles like a radio between stations.
No Purge left. I can hear colours now. That's probably a bad sign.
death: Tell the homestead I— [the entry ends here]
This is fine. This is f— [the entry ends here]
If you find this journal, the recipe for canteen stew is on the back page. Sorry about the stew. [the entry ends here]
Should have gone west. [the entry ends here]
revived: Woke up. Was I dead? The homestead paid to bring me back. I'm told there were forms.
Back from the dead. The afterlife had a waiting room. HALCY was the receptionist.
Revived. Feeling great. Feeling slightly haunted. Carrying on.
recalled: Radio says head home. You don't have to tell me twice. Well, you did, but I'm going.
Turning around. The homestead has a bunk with my name on it. Literally. I carved it.
Recalled. Packing up the souvenirs and hoofing it back.
Heading home. If anyone asks, I'm walking, not running. Mostly walking.
full: Pack's full. I physically cannot carry one more thing. Heading home.
I am more junk than person at this point. Time to go home.
Tried to fit one more tin can in my pack and the pack filed a complaint. Homeward.
body: [Recovered by the Halcyon Next-of-Kin Courier Service. Some items were lost in transit. HALCY apologises for the inconvenience.]
arrived: Home! The door opened. HALCY said 'Welcome back!' and I almost cried.
Back at the homestead. Never been so happy to see a door.
Made it home. Going to sleep for a week. Right after I unpack. Right after I sleep.
